description: Patch-level bumps of rumqttd are NOT automerged here, and the `//patch-automerge` preset is deliberately not extended. The reason is not risk in the role - the Molecule scenario would cover such a bump comfortably: it authenticates against the broker, refuses to pass unless an anonymous connection and a wrong password are declined, reads the listening sockets out of the container to prove the templated configuration is the one in force, asks the running binary its version and compares it against `rumqttd_version`, and pushes a message from one client to another. rumqttd keeps no state on disk, so there is nothing to migrate across a restart either.

The reason is that there is no patch stream to automerge. Upstream has published exactly two usable images for this role - `bytebeamio/rumqttd:0.18.0` and `:0.19.0` (the rest of Docker Hub is `latest`, which is the same digest as 0.19.0, and four 0.12.0 alpha/beta tags) - and rumqttd has not cut a patch release of any kind since 0.12.7 in March 2023. Everything since is `0.MINOR.0`, which Renovate's `semver` versioning classifies as a minor update, so a patch rule would match nothing that has ever existed. An automerge policy that can never fire is worse than none, because it reads as coverage that is not there.

The bigger problem the next person should know about is upstream's, not this role's: rumqttd 0.20.0 was released on 2025-09-29 and no container image was ever pushed for it. `build_rumqttd_docker.sh` in the rumqtt repository is a shell script a maintainer runs by hand, and the release workflow only uploads x86_64 binaries to GitHub Releases. The annotation in defaults/main.yml is therefore correct - `datasource=docker` tracks the only images that exist, and 0.19.0 is genuinely the newest one - but it has had nothing to propose since February 2024 and will keep having nothing until upstream pushes an image again. Pointing it at the GitHub releases instead would propose versions that cannot be pulled, which is why it stays where it is.
